data.title: rust-lang/rust Rust 1.98.0
data.author: rustbot
data.summary:
Language
Allow shortening lifetime of &mut when unsize-coercing, even in an invariant position. For example, you can now coerce a Cell to a Cell . Such shortenings were already previously allowed when coercing a &mut to a &, or coercing a & to a &.
Add deny-by-default invalidruntimesymboldefinitions lint and warn-by-default suspiciousruntimesymboldefinitions lint
The lints currently specifically targets core runtime symbols like memcmp, memset, strlen, ... and is planned to be expanded in the next few releases.
Add warn-by-default cvoidreturns lint to check core::ffi::cvoid as a return type
Platform Support
Add powerpc64-unknown-linux-gnuelfv2 as Tier 3
Add aarch64-unknown-linux-pauthtest as Tier 3 target
Promote thumbv7a-none-eabi to Tier 2
Promote thumbv7a-none-eabihf to Tier 2
Promote thumbv7r-none-eabi to Tier 2
Promote thumbv7r-none-eabihf to Tier 2
Promote thumbv8r-none-eabihf to Tier 2
Refer to Rust's platform support page for more information on Rust's tiered platform support.
Libraries
[Change Location lifetime to 'static in Panic[Hook]Info](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/146561)
Document panic in RangeInclusive::from(legacy::RangeInclusive)

The derive macro is available at {core,std}::derive. This was previously unintentionally stabilized in 1.96, but is now explicitly accepted as a stabilized API.
Please note that the MSRV for {core,std}::derive will be 1.96, and not 1.98.

data.title: nodejs/node 2026-10-29, Version 27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0 (Alpha), @RafaelGSS
data.author: RafaelGSS
data.summary:
Notable Changes
V8 15.6
The V8 engine is updated to version 15.6.75.13, up from 14.6 in Node.js 26. Highlights:
New language features enabled by default: Math.sumPrecise(), Intl.Locale.prototype.variants, Iterator.prototype.join(), Iterator.prototype.includes(), Iterator.zip() and Iterator.zipKeyed().
Experimental features behind flags: import defer (--js-defer-import-eval), Immutable ArrayBuffer (--js-immutable-arraybuffer) and RegExp buffer boundaries (--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries).
Memory: when --max-old-space-size is not set, the default heap size limit is now half of the physical memory clamped between 256 MB and 4 GB, and memory held by Buffer and ArrayBuffer instances now counts toward the heap limit. Applications that relied on the previous defaults should set --max-old-space-size explicitly.
Serialization: v8.serialize(), structuredClone() and postMessage() use a new format that older Node.js releases cannot read. v8.cachedDataVersionTag() and the compile cache also change on every Node.js patch of V8, not only on V8 version changes.
Observable behavior changes: Math methods now use LLVM's libm and may differ in the last bit; Math.random() sequences change for a given --random-seed; error.stack is no longer looked up through the prototype chain; await incurs fewer microtasks; Array.prototype.sort() uses PowerSort for large arrays and remains stable.
Heap snapshots include internal objects, numeric values and full script sources. Taking one takes about twice as long and the file is about twice as large.
WebAssembly: asm.js is no longer compiled to WebAssembly, and the --experimental-wasm- flags are renamed --wasm- .
A full changelog of the V8 changes between 14.6 and 15.6 will be shared soon.
Contributed by Joyee Cheung in #65161, #66537 and #66601.

data.author: richardlau
data.summary:
Notable Changes
This release marks the transition of Node.js 26.x into Long Term Support (LTS)
with the codename 'Lithium'. It will continue to receive updates through to
the end of April 2029.
Other than updating metadata, such as the process.release object, to reflect
that the release is LTS, no further changes from Node.js 26.12.1 are included.
If you are updating from an earlier Long Term Support release (e.g. Node.js 24
or 22 or earlier) please note that since Node.js 25 the official binaries for
Linux are linked against libatomic, which may need to be installed separately
depending on your Linux distribution.

data.author: astral-releases-bot[bot]
data.summary:
Release Notes
Released on 2026-10-21.
Following uv 0.13.4, which removed the affected eMudhra/emSign root from uv's own certificate store, this release updates the latest managed CPython builds for 3.11 and newer to python-build-standalone 20261021, including the CPython 3.15.1, 3.14.9, and 3.13.17 security patch releases. These builds include pip 26.2.2 both preinstalled in the managed interpreter and bundled with ensurepip, which installs pip by default when you run python -m venv. Both copies use certifi 2026.10.19, which removes the same affected root. After upgrading uv, run uv python upgrade to install the updated builds. Virtual environments pinned to an older Python patch version do not switch to the updated interpreter automatically. Upgrade pip separately in existing virtual environments.
Please note upstream CPython 3.9 and 3.10 still bundle pip releases whose certificate bundles trust the affected eMudhra/emSign root. We recommend migrating off of those versions and will no longer be releasing Docker images with uv installed for EOL Python versions.

data.author: astral-automations-bot[bot]
data.summary:
Release Notes
Released on 2026-10-09.
The executables in our macOS and Windows release archives and ruff wheels are now code-signed. macOS executables are signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. Windows executables have timestamped Authenticode signatures from Azure Artifact Signing. This enables verification of the release publisher and binary integrity, supports publisher-based allowlisting, and should reduce security warnings and antivirus false positives.
Breaking changes
Update the default and latest Python versions for 3.15 (#28792)
Ruff now defaults to Python 3.11 instead of 3.10 when no Python version is configured through target-version or requires-python. When checking for syntax errors without a configured Python version, Ruff now defaults to Python 3.15 instead of 3.14.
Update the default rule set (#28786)
Several of the flake8-datetimez rules (DTZ001, DTZ005, DTZ006, DTZ007, DTZ011, DTZ012, and DTZ901) are no longer enabled by default, while undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage (F406), which corresponds to a syntax error, is now enabled by default.
Update Rust crate quick-junit to 0.8.0 (#27295)
JUnit output now uses a skipped attribute instead of disabled on elements and includes a skipped attribute on the root element.
[flake8-import-conventions] Add datetime as dt as a conventional alias (ICN001) (#28790)
Support Unicode dummy variable names (#28722)
The default lint.dummy-variable-rgx now recognizes underscore-prefixed Unicode names, such as 次, as dummy variables.
Update to Unicode 17 (#21229, #28784)
Ruff now uses Unicode 17 data for identifier normalization and named character escapes ("\N{...}").
Always show unsafe and display-only fixes in the CLI (#27810)
The default full output format now shows unsafe fixes and suggestions requiring manual review, regardless of the unsafe-fixes setting. Actually applying unsafe fixes still requires explicit opt-in.
